learningObjectives: Apply everything from Lessons 1-8 in one consolidated, more complex Template: TestSheets, Templates, linking Values, Conditions, and price verification.
Build a data-driven test that configures and orders a customized computer, verifying the calculated price at every step.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Grand Scenario: Order Your Own Computer

elements.description: Independent hypothetical capstone: model configurable computer choices, expected prices and negative combinations in a data-driven Template. The following prices and restrictions are exercise assumptions, not verified current shop catalogue data or original Academy material.

elements.text: Calculate expected values from the agreed hypothetical price specification, then compare the SUT output through appropriate Verify assertions. Computing the expectation in Tosca does not mean the SUT itself has calculated correctly.

rows: Office Suite = standard · Image Viewer = +$5.00 · Office Suite (alt) = +$100.00 · Another Office Suite = +$40.00 (only ONE Office Suite allowed per order)
COD (Cash on Delivery) only — remember its surcharge in the Total price calculation

elements.title: TestCase flow
items: Use a non-production test environment with synthetic customer data.
Confirm or scan the controls and actions required by the agreed exercise specification.
Map computer choices and expected prices into the Template.
Verify invalid combinations are rejected and retain required cleanup.
For the valid path, compare independently calculated subtotal and all specified fees with the observed total.
Generate and inspect concrete cases, then trial-run assertions before organized execution.

elements.text: Independent rule for this exercise: selecting both office suites is invalid. Verify the expected rejection, omit order completion and perform cleanup. Simply logging out without verifying rejection would not prove correct validation.
No original workspace subset is bundled or verified here. Inspect the actual Modules in your workspace; folder names and module availability are not guaranteed.

elements.title: Independent planning checklist
items: Define the exact valid and invalid configurations and their expected outcomes.
Include delivery and payment fees only when the hypothetical specification requires them; do not assume a current live price or tax rate.
Use expected-output Attributes with the intended Verify values.
Keep synthetic credentials outside literal repeated step values using an appropriate scoped configuration source.
Inspect source links, generation conditions and actual Module availability.

elements.text: Original Academy Grand Scenario files, subset contents and solution video were inaccessible and remain unverified. This local page provides an independent hypothetical capstone, not a PDF viewer, original download or certified solution.

examPitfalls.title: Exercise assumptions are not live catalogue facts
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating example prices and module folders as the current SUT contract.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Agree and verify the actual specification before implementing a real test.

examPitfalls.title: A skipped checkout is not validation proof
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Logging out on invalid data without checking the rejection.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Assert the specified rejection and preserve required cleanup.

examPitfalls.title: Expected price must be independent
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using only the observed total as both actual and expected.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Calculate from the agreed rules and compare with the SUT output.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Under this independent exercise’s hypothetical price table, what is the expensive package’s base price?

options.text: There is no base price — it's calculated purely from add-ons.

practiceQuiz.hint: The 'Cheap computer' is the standard-priced option at $800.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The local hypothetical specification sets the base to 1,800; this does not verify a current catalogue price.

optionExplanations.A: The exercise table specifies a base package price as well as add-ons.
optionExplanations.B: Eight hundred is the hypothetical cheap package base.
optionExplanations.C: One thousand is not the exercise’s expensive package base.
optionExplanations.D: Eighteen hundred is the local hypothetical base, not a current live price claim.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The independent specification rejects a configuration with both office suites. Which negative-test behavior establishes that expected outcome?

options.text: Pause and prompt the user to choose one manually.
Verify the expected rejection, omit order completion and perform the required cleanup.
Automatically remove one of the two Office Suites and continue.
Proceed through checkout and add both surcharges to the Total.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario states only one Office Suite can be bought with the same system.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The invalid rule requires an assertion of rejection; skipping checkout alone is not evidence that the SUT rejects the input.

optionExplanations.A: A manual choice does not assert the specified automatic rejection.
optionExplanations.B: This verifies the negative outcome and keeps the required cleanup.
optionExplanations.C: Silently repairing the invalid input no longer tests the rejection rule.
optionExplanations.D: Completing the invalid order contradicts the agreed exercise rule.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the independent data layout, which proposed Attribute path holds the expected product subtotal?

options.text: Precondition >> Customer >> Type of User >> Email
Verification >> Product Price
Instance.Character
Workflow >> Payment Method >> Credit Card

practiceQuiz.hint: It's under the Verification branch of the TestSheet, not Precondition.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The local exercise proposes Verification > Product Price for expected subtotal data, not a universal Tosca reserved path.

optionExplanations.A: Email is login input, not the proposed expected subtotal.
optionExplanations.B: This is the proposed expected-output path in the independent layout.
optionExplanations.C: Character describes input validity, not the product price.
optionExplanations.D: Payment method data is not the proposed subtotal Attribute.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The hypothetical specification includes delivery and COD fees. Which additional terms belong in the expected total?

options.text: A fixed 10% tax applied to every order.
Any surcharge from the chosen delivery method and the COD payment method.
The Discount Code surcharge, which always applies.
Nothing else — only feature surcharges affect the Total.

practiceQuiz.hint: Two extra sources of surcharge are called out in the hints.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Include the specified delivery/payment fees alongside configured product prices; do not invent a universal tax or fee.

optionExplanations.A: No universal ten-percent tax was specified.
optionExplanations.B: The stated delivery and COD fees are terms in the expected total.
optionExplanations.C: The example does not specify a universal discount-code surcharge.
optionExplanations.D: This ignores the explicitly specified additional fees.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which earlier independent pattern can guide this exercise’s price assertions and positive/negative paths?

options.text: None — it's a completely new structure.
The Shirt Size TestCase from Lesson 1.
The API country/ID TestCase from Lesson 8.
The Discount Code TestCase from Lesson 7.

practiceQuiz.hint: Both involve verifying a calculated price/value against valid vs invalid conditions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The local discount example also combines expected price rules with selected positive/negative paths; this does not certify an original exercise hint.

optionExplanations.A: Useful model/mapping/price patterns can be reused without copying a whole test.
optionExplanations.B: A simple size-selection example does not cover the same calculated-price pattern.
optionExplanations.C: Country/ID API verification is not the earlier price-rule pattern.
optionExplanations.D: The independent discount pattern supplies relevant assertions and path-selection concepts.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How should you establish which Modules are available for a real implementation of this independent exercise?

options.text: Inspect your actual Module inventory and identification; reuse suitable Modules or scan missing controls.
Assume every course installation has the same provided subset.
Execution >> ExecutionLists >> Grand Scenario.
Requirements >> DemoWebShop >> Computers.

practiceQuiz.hint: Do not infer workspace contents from an inaccessible original file.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Module availability and folder names depend on the actual workspace; inspect existing models before creating new ones.

optionExplanations.A: Actual inventory and identification determine whether existing Modules can be reused.
optionExplanations.B: An inaccessible subset is not evidence that its Modules exist in this workspace.
optionExplanations.C: Execution containers arrange tests rather than hold scanned control models.
optionExplanations.D: Requirements describe criteria rather than the technical Module inventory.
